Cumulative number of distinct (robot maker, customer organization) pairs for which a source documents a general-purpose robot doing production work for that named external customer, autonomously as reported (provisional pioneering-stage KPI, owner 2026-10-18). Monthly (obs = month; the current month in progress), the count among events published by the month's end; derived by gather/collectors/robots_hardware.py from events carrying a `deployment` case (ledger.deployment_roster); intake stages such events, verify checks them. A case is {maker, platform, customer, job, status, form?, site?, robots?, autonomy?}; status working = the source documents the work; ended = the source says it stopped (still counted, marked ended); disputed = a credible source (the customer, on-site reporters, a regulator) contradicts it (not counted until a later working event; on one day a dispute wins). It counts from its first working event's publication date. Rules for a working case: (R1) general-purpose = a humanoid (legged, wheeled or column-based) or mobile manipulator, i.e. it can move itself between workstations AND it physically handles the objects the job is about; not fixed arms or cells whatever AI runs them, vehicles/AMRs/forklifts, robots used only as sensor carriers, exoskeletons. (R2) production work for a NAMED external customer organization, and the source says what job the robot does there: a pilot inside live operations counts; not the maker's own or affiliated facilities, labs, showrooms, demos or livestreams outside live operations, non-production tests, on-site training/'practical training' (实训/实习)/validation, testbed centres, orders/contracts/plans, units delivered without reported work, or a bare mention of the customer in a list of sites, users or hours. (R3) the source says the robot works autonomously (autonomous, on its own, without remote control, 全自主, 零遥操 ...): `autonomy` quotes those words; silence about teleoperation is not enough. Claims are trusted unless credibly disputed. (R4) maker = the robot maker (not the AI-model provider); customer = the parent organization (one pair however many sites, robots, jobs or robot generations; a new pair needs a different maker or customer). robots = the disclosed count, else null. Record each new pair once (its earliest qualifying source), later changes as new events with relates (status ended/disputed, or working with new robots/site/job).
